primary_evidence.author: Kitahara Jirota
primary_evidence.section: Bus announcements, item 3, lines189-190; Saru basis line241
primary_evidence.supports: hi ka an expresses possible occurrence of a bus stopping suddenly, not the driver's ability or passengers' permission. Both current reviewers read the primary article.
wa an / plural wa oka expresses result state.
ari is the plural-object counterpart of anu; the retained-placement predicate uses a=ari wa oka.

Prior separately accepted coordinate dialogue uses a=ukaomare for intentional image overlap and a=ari for plural placed images. Current negative snap clause is a new reviewed composition, not automatic transfer of whole prior acceptance.
eaykap after finite verb expresses impossibility; here actual UI rejection, not possible automatic movement.
uneno refers to sameness of qualities/situation; equal quantity/degree is specifically upakno.
sinep sinep is distributive one by one/each, supporting per-image scope in retained percentage explanation.
Productive verb + okere completion, in primary narrative (canoe overturn completed). The UI result-comparison is a current composition, not an attested software phrase.
Existence/location predicate and equal degree/size comparison.
